Elon Musk calling Raptor 3 “kind of alien technology” is spot on 🚀
He shared how even top propulsion pros looked at a photo of the Raptor 3 and went, “Wait, this engine looks unfinished—it’s missing stuff!”
Then came the reveal: “Nope, that’s the full thing… and it’s firing with efficiency levels we’ve never seen before.”
This isn’t just an upgrade—it’s a total game-changer for rocket engines:
•  Ditches the traditional base heat shield entirely → slashes weight, boosts long-term reliability during re-entry
•  Minor fuel leaks? No panic—they vent straight into the open plasma and burn off harmlessly (unlike older boxed designs where they’d be a disaster)
•  Unlocks way higher payload to orbit, better fuel efficiency, and overall rocket performance
•  Radically fewer components and a cleaner layout, yet it delivers massively more power and capability
•  Secondary cooling loops, sensors, and electronics are all baked right into the engine’s structure—no external clutter, everything protected and streamlined
Pure first-principles brilliance from the SpaceX team. This thing looks minimalist because it had to evolve beyond legacy thinking. Starship V3 with Raptor 3 is going to be insane.

RAPTOR 3: THE MOST ADVANCED ROCKET ENGINE EVER BUILT – ELON MUSK ON ITS INSANE POWER & PRECISION

Raptor 3 is SpaceX’s latest evolution of the methane-fueled, full-flow staged combustion engine powering Starship. It’s a massive leap in design: fully integrated regenerative cooling (no external heat shield needed), simplified architecture with far fewer parts, record thrust-to-weight ratio, higher chamber pressure, and dramatically improved reliability—all while pushing thrust targets well beyond previous versions.

This engine is what makes Starship V3/V4 the most powerful rocket system in history, capable of rapid reusability and the massive payload/fleet cadence required for Mars colonization.

Elon Musk on Raptor 3’s mind-blowing scale and precision:

“Raptor 3 engine is very advanced engine, by far the best rocket engine ever made. On liftoff, Starship is generating over 100 gigawatts of power. It’s 20% of US, while not exploding. There’s thousands of ways it could explode and only one way that it doesn’t.”

Key highlights of Raptor 3:
•Extreme power density — A single Starship stack with 33 sea-level + vacuum Raptors produces more power than entire power plants—over 100 GW at liftoff—equivalent to ~20% of the entire U.S. electrical grid’s output, yet it stays intact.
•No heat shield — Full regenerative cooling channels through the engine structure eliminate the need for external shielding, slashing complexity, weight, and refurbishment time.
•Simplified & reliable — Fewer joints, integrated plumbing, and stainless-steel construction make it easier to build at scale and more tolerant of the extreme conditions of launch, reentry, and reuse.
•Path to Mars — Higher thrust, better Isp, and rapid turnaround enable orbital refueling, heavy-lift Moon missions, and the hundreds of flights needed to bootstrap a self-sustaining city on Mars.
Raptor 3 isn’t incremental—it’s the engine that turns “possible” into “routine” for interplanetary travel. Every test fire brings us closer to the day Starship fleets launch daily.
Which Raptor 3 breakthrough hits hardest—the 100 GW liftoff power, the shield-less design, or the sheer engineering precision to avoid exploding? Let’s keep igniting the future. 🚀🔥🛠️
